To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photonic crystals of the scales of some butterfly species have iridescent reflection spectra, that the iridescence is suppressed by the presence of a thin film on the scales, and that this thin film has an index of refraction close to that of air. Proc. SPIE 4425, Photonic Crystal Materials and Devices, (26 April 2001); doi: 10.1117/12.425799 David R. S. Cumming

(i) the iridescent color of the butterfly is due to the reflection of light by the photonic crystals, (ii) the photonic crystals are three dimensional, (iii) the iridescence is suppressed by a combination of the structure of the crystal, the orientation of the crystals in the scales, the thickness of the scales and their shape, (iv) the photonic bandgaps of these crystals have been calculated and are in the visible range.

iridescence from photogenic structures is suppressed in butterfly scales because of the presence of an additional structure, the so-called “ground layer”, and that the ground layer has a thickness of a half of the wavelength of light in air.

the physics of photonic crystals and how they are exploited for coloration in nature.
the study of the physical properties of the scales in butterflies and the relation of these properties to the structure of the scales.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scales are photonic crystals that suppress iridescence by the mechanism of bandgap formation.
the iridescence from the photonic structures is a consequence of their three-dimensional periodicity.

the iridescence of butterfly scales arises from a combination of photonic crystal and thin film interference effects, and that the iridiscence suppression in the scales of Morpho species is due to an increase in the thickness of the scale and the presence of a thin film of melanin on top of the scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the iridescence of butterfly scales is not a simple phenomenon.

the photonic crystal properties of these structures can be understood and predicted by standard methods, but the details of their development and evolution are not yet understood and are the subject of ongoing research.
the iridescence in these structures is due to the presence of a photonic bandgap and its suppression is due to the absence of the bandgap.
